task: research and price a used car as a buyer: set the search filters that matter (make/model, year range, budget, mileage, drivetrain), browse the matching listings, open a specific listing and check its history and price rating, and get a price estimate or value for a specific vehicle; complete when a specific car's listing with its price evaluation (e.g. good/fair deal rating or KBB value) is on screen. Surface pinned: a used-car marketplace or pricing site (KBB, CarGurus, Carvana, AutoTrader, Edmunds). Variants: car-dealer/dealership-side content, car-flipping or reselling business content, car review vlogs with driving footage, and mechanic-inspection videos do not belong.

tree.label: Research and price a used car
tree.note: 1 on every site and tool the session opens - most open several. 2 then 3 on a marketplace, with 3.5 sending the search back into 2.10 when the list is too long, too short or wrongly ordered. 4 on an opened listing, 4.9 where a history link exists. 5 where a value is wanted - fed from 4.8 when the car is a listing, from memory when it is the user's own car. 6 is the loop most keepers run: it re-runs 2 to 4 on the next site or 5 on the next tool and carries the numbers between them. 7 after any 4 or 5, and again after 6. 8 in three keepers only. The task as asked ends at 7.

children.label: Reach the car site
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 on every site; 1.3 whenever a prompt appears, which is at any point in the task; 1.4 when the site has a country edition. 1.5 is never done on camera.

questions.question: Does the price on the opened listing match the price shown in the preview?

questions.question: Is the advertised mileage realistic for the vehicle's age, or could it be a typo?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might overvalue the car based on an impossibly low mileage figure, failing to apply the common sense needed to spot a seller's typo.
questions.check: What year and mileage does the listing show, and is the mileage far below what that age would carry?

questions.question: Does the savings figure equal the value minus the asking price?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the math behind the advertised deal to ensure the platform isn't misrepresenting the actual savings.
questions.check: What estimated value, asking price, and savings figure does the listing show, and does value minus price equal the savings?
questions.say_example: It claims <2,000> in savings. The value and the price are only <1,200> apart. The savings number is padded.

questions.question: Does the price gauge put this price below, within, or above the fair range?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the intuitive visual context of whether the asking price is at the very top, middle, or bottom of the acceptable market range.

questions.question: Should you swipe through the full image galleries for these listings?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent relying solely on the text metadata might select a car that lacks the specific premium features you requested.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks handing over cash for a vehicle they cannot legally register or insure because the agent failed to verify the legal legitimacy of the seller's title status.
questions.check: For a private seller, does the description say the title is in hand, clean, and in the seller's name?
questions.say_example: This is a private seller. The ad doesn't say they hold the title. Ask before you go see it, or the transfer can get stuck.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether it is worth your time to contact the seller for the missing VIN or if you should just move on to a more detailed listing.
